key_insight: Adults with weaker preoperative social connection had worse postoperative survival-related outcomes in several analyses, especially early mortality and non-home discharge.
clinical_relevance: Social connection may serve as a useful preoperative prognostic marker when identifying patients at higher postoperative risk, though the evidence is still low certainty.
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of adult surgical studies with preoperative social connection measures
Databases searched: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycInfo, and CENTRAL through July 17, 2026
Random-effects REML models with modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; risk of bias assessed with QUIPS and certainty with prognostic GRADE
evidence_signal: From 445 included studies, only 72 contributed poolable estimates; the primary survival analysis was not statistically clear (HR 1.37, 95% CI 0.99-1.89, very low certainty), while early mortality and non-home discharge showed associations.
watch_item: Most evidence came from marital status and observational cohorts, so social connection may be confounded by other factors and should not be treated as a stand-alone decision rule.
paper_title: Preoperative Social Connection and Postoperative Outcomes in Adults Undergoing Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
